summary.headline: FY26 value added revenue rose 12.3% to INR49,180 million with a record 18.8% EBITDA margin; Q4 EBITDA up 17.6% to INR2,573 million.
summary.overview: Management reported its best full year yet: FY26 VAR grew 12.3% to INR49,180 million, EBITDA rose 13.5% to INR9,255 million, and EBITDA margin reached a record 18.8% of VAR. Q4 VAR grew 17.5% to INR14,058 million, with EBITDA margin stable at 18.3% despite geopolitical cost pressures. Advanced Ride Technologies drove growth (FY26 up 19.7%), while Clean Air and Powertrain grew only 5.5% for the year. Lifetime order book stood at INR124,000 million at March 31, 2026, with exports and new Clean Air and bearings wins cited as growth drivers.

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,296 million, up 5.5% YoY; Q4 INR6,905 million, up 9.9%. Growth tepid due to OEM and within-OEM mix shifts (lower-end SUVs, EV mix at a European OEM), not share loss per management.

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (suspension)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,885 million, up 19.7% YoY; Q4 INR7,153 million, up 26%. DCx DaVinci mechanical suspension adopted by a leading Indian OEM for a flagship SUV.

guidance_outlook: Lifetime order book of INR124,000 million gives 100% visibility of FY2028 internal revenue target; management expects double-digit medium-term growth.
Export order book expected to keep growing; current exports are about 5-6% of sales versus a 14-20% share of the order book (as stated).
New West India shock absorber plant (board-approved) expected to take 6-12 months to commission; peak revenue contribution expected mid-2028 to 2029.
Clean Air entry into the largest Indian PV OEM's supplier panel for a Gasoline Particulate Filter; growth expected from late FY27/FY28.
Management expects margins to remain stable going forward.
Addressable Clean Air content from CAFE 3 and BS7 estimated at INR1,300-1,400 crore over the next three to five years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex of about INR1,400 million across the North India Clean Air facility (announced Q3 FY26) and a new greenfield West India Advanced Ride Technologies plant.
FY26 capex was about INR1,150 million.
Bearings business: new plant not yet decided; management is checking whether existing plants can accommodate the new bearings business.
Capex-to-steady-state revenue ratio cited as roughly 1:3.
Localization about 89-90%, management intends to keep it near 90% over the long term.
demand_pricing: Management says the DCx DaVinci suspension has 3-4 OEMs interested, including Indian, Japanese, Korean and European OEMs; it targets about 50% of India's roughly 5-5.5 million PV market.
Conventional mechanical dampers still dominate over 90% of Indian passenger vehicles.
Export drivers cited: technology equalization (BS6.2 with RDE, Euro 6 RDE), China-plus-one sourcing, labour cost advantage and rupee depreciation.

Direct material cost (steel) recovered through quarterly escalator agreements; indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, fuel) being recovered through customer negotiations, which management says can be tough.
Management said currency depreciation gives an immediate 15-20% improvement in global competitiveness.

qa_highlights.question: How will exports ramp over the next two to three years, and when will the new plants and bearings orders commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are described as middle-ended, with a critical mass around 2028 and ramp starting 2027-28. The West India plant takes 6-12 months to commission; peak around mid-2028 to 2029. Bearings value not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is content per vehicle for commercial vehicle exhaust systems versus passenger vehicles, and how do diesel, petrol, CNG and hybrid differ?
qa_highlights.answer: A commercial exhaust is 3-4x a passenger car system and can reach 10x for tractors with aftertreatment. Diesel carries higher hot-end content. Hybrids can lift content from 1x to 1.5-2x. CNG and hybrid need exhaust systems with no content loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports go directly to third-party OEMs or only to Tenneco group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports go both to Tenneco group entities and to third-party OEMs with group permission, which management frames as partnership, not competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why no two-wheeler suspension or Clean Air two-wheeler presence, and is the CV localization point about Clean Air?
qa_highlights.answer: Management avoids low-margin two- and three-wheelers and will enter only with technology differentiation; M&A also being considered. The CV localization reference relates to Clean Air, with localization about 89-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Clean Air growth tepid and what drives the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was held back by absence from the largest PV OEM and by mix shifts at existing OEMs. Margins attributed to the P3 operating model, standardized Lego-brick product design, and a higher-margin export order book; management expects margins to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: How do OEMs upgrade from passive to passive-plus or DaVinci suspension, and what is the cost delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Upgrades within mechanical suspension fit the existing packaging envelope with small cost delta. Electronics and software (semi-active CVSA) above about INR35 lakh MSRP need routing and ECU changes, which raise cost substantially.

qa_highlights.question: How are currency movements and indirect cost inflation handled in export contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Currency depreciation is seen as a benefit. Indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, LPG, CNG, crude) are being bundled and recovered from customers, with cost-cutting in SG&A and factory efficiency as mitigation.

risks_watch: Clean Air growth lagged the market in FY26 due to OEM mix shifts and absence from the largest PV OEM until FY28.
Indirect cost inflation (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, fuel) from the Middle East situation; recovery from customers may be contested.
Timing of export ramp, West India plant commissioning and bearings capacity decision.
FY26 PAT absorbed a one-time labour code charge; quarterly margin sustainability depends on cost recovery.
Rising Clean Air volumes depend on CAFE 3 and BS7 content gains and on EV/hybrid mix shifts in global markets.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and suspension technology, with frequent references to best-ever results. Less specific on bearings value, plant timing and Clean Air near-term growth, where explanations leaned on mix and future programs.

Importantly, we achieved our highest ever EBITDA margin of 18.8%, expanding by 21 points over the last year.
As of March 31, 2026, our lifetime order book stands at INR124,000 million after accounting for net additions and programs that commenced production this year.
